issues.reason: (Measure <entity> <scale> <magnitude> <unit>) puts an absolute value on a dimension, so (Measure (sk_lower_heart $x) risk 88 percent) falsely says the lowering event's risk IS 88 percent rather than that the risk falls BY 88 percent.

"the scientists" is a definite plural and "claim" is a distributive predicate, and Quantifiers, generics & scope requires the same rule form over (PartOf $x <group>) alongside the group event for a grouped plural ("the dogs barked").

gaps_confirmed: no carrier for a measured CHANGE on an event ("lower X by N percent") — Measure is absolute, MoreBy compares two entities, and percentages otherwise appear only as (Fraction p 100) inside partitives
sealing is specified for propositions (one atom, or several under And); a quantified Implication with its own strength/quantifier force has no defined behaviour inside a seal
the remote/hypothetical conditional "if X V-ed, Y would V" — only the indicative Implication rule and the past-perfect subjunctive Counterfactual are specified
new_gaps: distributing a definite-plural attitude verb whose complement is itself a rule forces an Implication nested inside a seal inside a rule consequent, and nothing states how the inner rule's variable avoids capture by the outer rule's range variable
repair_summary: Removed (Measure (sk_lower_heart $x) risk 88 percent) and (Measure (sk_lower_stroke $x) risk 80 percent) — no licensed encoding for a percentage reduction, so the offending atoms are dropped rather than replaced. Added td1_claim_dist, the per-member distribution rule over (PartOf $s sk_scientist_1) at (STV 1.0 0.9), carrying the same sealed complement; the outer range variable is $s so it does not capture the sealed rule's $x.
notes: The 88/80 percent figures are simply lost — that is the correct outcome under "removing a false atom is a fix; replacing it with an invention is not". Everything else (sealing under claim's Theme, the projected definite pill, the tenseless subjunctive clauses, the heart_attack genus) is left byte-identical.
